title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analysis reveals a lactate-driven crosstalk between NFATc4(+) tumor cells and SPP1(+) macrophages in glioblastoma.
authors: Wang, Ruoli; Wu, Wantao; Wu, Xuan; Yuan, Ye; Zhang, Zhongyi; Chen, Junyi; Xie, Yuxin; Zhang, Linhui; Yu, Xinrui; Zhang, Hao; Xie, Zongyi
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用单细胞与空间转录组及机器学习分析GBM中乳酸代谢相关转录因子NFATc4与巨噬细胞互作，但核心是肿瘤微环境与预后模型，缺乏蛋白质-DNA结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘涉及TF。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains a lethal brain tumor with limited therapeutic options. Metabolic reprogramming, particularly lactate metabolism, plays a critical role in tumor progression and immune evasion. METHODS: Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to investigate the heterogeneity of lactate metabolism in GBM. RESULTS: Using scRNA-seq data (GSE138794), we classified neoplastic cells into high- and low-lactate subgroups and identified nuclear factor of activated T-cells cytoplasmic 4 (NFATc4) as a key transcription factor associated with elevated lactate metabolism. Pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed dynamic upregulation of NFATc4 during neoplastic cell differentiation, correlating with invasive phenotypes. Spatial transcriptomics (GSE194329) demonstrated colocalization of NFATc4(+) tumor cells with SPP1(+) macrophages, suggesting their microenvironmental crosstalk. A prognostic model constructed via 101 machine-learning algorithms (StepCox[forward] + RSF) achieved favorable performance across independent cohorts (TCGA, CGGA, GSE108474, GSE4412, and meta-cohort). Patients with different risk levels showed distinct immune infiltration, copy number alterations, and drug-sensitivity profiles. In vitro functional assays confirmed that NFATc4 knockdown in GBM cells suppressed tumor cell proliferation, migration, and cell cycle while promoting apoptosis. Besides, NFATc4 knockdown in GBM cells reduced SPP1 expression, migration, and M2-like polarization of co-cultured macrophages. Moreover, silencing SPP1 in macrophages attenuated the pro-tumorigenic effects on co-cultured GBM cells, validating the functional relevance of the NFATc4-SPP1 axis. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals lactate metabolism-related NFATc4 as a promising therapeutic target in GBM, with implications for prognosis stratification and combination therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景：胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）仍是一种治疗选择有限的致死性脑肿瘤。代谢重编程，尤其是乳酸代谢，在肿瘤进展和免疫逃逸中发挥关键作用。方法：本研究整合了单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）、空间转录组学和机器学习，以探究GBM中乳酸代谢的异质性。结果：利用scRNA-seq数据（GSE138794），我们将肿瘤细胞分为高乳酸和低乳酸亚群，并鉴定出活化T细胞核因子胞质4（NFATc4）为与高乳酸代谢相关的关键转录因子。伪时间轨迹分析显示，在肿瘤细胞分化过程中NFATc4动态上调，并与侵袭性表型相关。空间转录组学（GSE194329）显示NFATc4(+)肿瘤细胞与SPP1(+)巨噬细胞共定位，提示其微环境串扰。通过101种机器学习算法（StepCox[forward] + RSF）构建的预后模型在独立队列（TCGA、CGGA、GSE108474、GSE4412和meta-cohort）中取得了良好性能。不同风险水平的患者表现出不同的免疫浸润、拷贝数变异和药物敏感性特征。体外功能实验证实，GBM细胞中NFATc4敲低抑制了肿瘤细胞增殖、迁移和细胞周期，同时促进凋亡。此外，GBM细胞中NFATc4敲低降低了共培养巨噬细胞的SPP1表达、迁移和M2样极化。而且，巨噬细胞中沉默SPP1减弱了对共培养GBM细胞的促肿瘤效应，验证了NFATc4-SPP1轴的功能相关性。结论：我们的研究揭示了乳酸代谢相关的NFATc4作为GBM中有前景的治疗靶点，对预后分层和联合治疗具有意义。
